pick-and-pull: Gain advantage on action rolls to pick nonmagical locks, disarm nonmagical traps, or steal items from a target (by stealth or force).
rain-of-blades:
Spend a Hope to make a Spellcast Roll and conjure throwing blades that strike all targets within Very Close range. Targets you succeed against take {{proficiency|#d8+2 magic damage|d8+2 magic damage using your Proficiency}}.
A Vulnerable target you hit takes an extra 1d8 damage.
uncanny-disguise:
When you have a few minutes to prepare, mark a Stress to don the facade of any humanoid you can picture clearly. While disguised, you have advantage on Presence Rolls to avoid scrutiny.
Place {{spellcast|# tokens|tokens equal to your Spellcast trait}} on this card; spend one when you take an action while disguised. After the action that spends the last token, the disguise drops.
midnight-spirit:
Spend a Hope to summon a humanoid-sized spirit that can move or carry things for you until your next rest.
You can also send it to attack: make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Very Far range. On a success, the spirit moves into Melee range with the target, and you roll {{spellcast|#d6|a number of d6s equal to your Spellcast trait}} and deal that much magic damage. The spirit then dissipates. You can have only one spirit at a time.
shadowbind: Make a Spellcast Roll against all adversaries within Very Close range. Targets you succeed against are temporarily Restrained as their shadow binds them in place.
chokehold:
When you position yourself behind a creature about your size, mark a Stress to pull them into a chokehold, making them temporarily Vulnerable.
When a creature attacks a target Vulnerable this way, they deal an extra 2d6 damage.
veil-of-night: Make a Spellcast Roll (13). On a success, create a temporary curtain of darkness between two points within Far range. Only you can see through it. You’re Hidden to adversaries on the other side and have advantage on attacks you make through it. It remains until you cast another spell.
stealth-expertise:
When you roll with Fear while trying to move unnoticed through a dangerous area, mark a Stress to roll with Hope instead.
If an ally within Close range is also moving unnoticed and rolls with Fear, mark a Stress to change their result to a roll with Hope.
glyph-of-nightfall: Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Very Close range. On a success, spend a Hope to conjure a dark glyph on their body that exposes their weak points, temporarily reducing their Difficulty by {{knowledgeMin1|#|a value equal to your Knowledge (minimum 1)}}.
hush:
Make a Spellcast Roll against a target within Close range. On a success, spend a Hope to conjure suppressive magic around the target, covering everything within Very Close range of them and following them as they move.
The target and anything in the area is Silenced until the GM spends a Fear on their turn to clear it, you cast Hush again, or you take Major damage. While Silenced, they can’t make noise or cast spells.
phantom-retreat: Spend a Hope to activate Phantom Retreat where you stand. Spend another Hope any time before your next rest to disappear and reappear where you activated it. The spell ends after you reappear.
dark-whispers:
Speak into the mind of anyone you’ve made physical contact with; once a channel is open, they can speak back. You can also mark a Stress to make a Spellcast Roll against them. On a success, ask the GM one of these questions and receive an answer:
- Where are they?
- What are they doing?
- What are they afraid of?
- What do they cherish most in the world?
mass-disguise:
With a few minutes of silence to focus, mark a Stress to change the appearance of all willing creatures within Close range. New forms must share a general body structure and size, and can be someone or something you’ve seen or entirely fabricated. A disguised creature has advantage on Presence Rolls to avoid scrutiny.
Activate a Countdown (8), ticking down as a consequence the GM chooses. When it triggers, the disguise drops.
midnight-touched:
When 4 or more loadout cards are from the Midnight domain, gain:
- Once per rest, when you have 0 Hope and the GM would gain a Fear, gain a Hope instead.
- When you make a successful attack, mark a Stress to add the result of your Fear Die to your damage roll.
vanishing-dodge: When an attack against you that would deal physical damage fails, spend a Hope to envelop yourself in shadow, becoming Hidden and teleporting to a point within Close range of the attacker. You stay Hidden until your next action roll.
shadowhunter: While shrouded in low light or darkness, gain a +1 bonus to your Evasion and make attack rolls with advantage.
spellcharge:
When you take magic damage, place tokens equal to the Hit Points you marked on this card, up to {{spellcast|#|your Spellcast trait}}.
When you succeed on an attack, spend any number of tokens to add a d6 per token to your damage roll.
night-terror: Once per long rest, choose any targets within Very Close range to perceive you as a nightmarish horror. They must succeed on a Reaction Roll (16) or become temporarily Horrified, making them Vulnerable. Steal Fear from the GM equal to the number of Horrified targets (up to the Fear in the GM’s pool), roll that many d6s, deal the total to each Horrified target, and discard the stolen Fear.
twilight-toll:
Choose a target within Far range. When you succeed on an action roll against them that doesn’t result in a damage roll, place a token on this card. When you deal damage to this target, spend any number of tokens to add a d12 per token to your damage roll. You can hold Twilight Toll on only one creature at a time.
When you choose a new target or take a rest, clear unspent tokens.
eclipse:
Make a Spellcast Roll (16). Once per long rest on a success, plunge everything within Far range into complete darkness that only you and your allies can see through. Attack rolls against you or an ally in the shadow have disadvantage, and when you or an ally succeeds with Hope against an adversary in it, the target marks a Stress.
This lasts until the GM spends a Fear on their turn to clear it or you take Severe damage.
specter-of-the-dark: Mark a Stress to become Spectral until you make an action roll targeting another creature. While Spectral, you’re immune to physical damage and can float and pass through solid objects. Other creatures can still see you.
